text: The Sun is terrible at its job.
Its core is fifteen million degrees. And one cubic metre of it makes about as much heat as a compost heap.
You make more heat than that. Per cubic metre, you are out-performing a star.
So how does a compost heap light up the whole solar system?
Fusion. But fusion is hard. Protons are all positive, so they shove each other away.
The only way through is to cheat. Quantum tunnelling. Physics for: walking through the wall anyway.
It's so unlikely, the average proton waits about nine billion years for its turn.
But the Sun has so many protons, it still pulls this off about a hundred trillion trillion trillion times a second.
And that slowness is the secret. If fusion were easy, the Sun would have burned out before life ever began.
So the Sun isn't lazy. It's pacing itself.
